notes: Why it stayed on the tab. Buddy only knew the clicks of a browser started with --remote-debugging-port. A script that presses things through Windows itself (UI Automation, no port, your mouse never moves) was not heard. Every new page title also put the pointer back on the tab, and a browser window that keeps itself on top hid the pointer for up to 2 s.

Now. Buddy hears those presses in Chrome and Edge and the pointer flies to the thing that was pressed. After a click it stays there for 10 s while the page changes. With every new step the pointer is put above all windows at once.
The trace (%APPDATA%\Buddy\crew\trace.log) has a line for each press, for example CLICK ... a link at (2130, 1253). Only the kind of thing and the place, never a text.

What it cannot show. A thing that is gone in the instant it is pressed (a back button that takes its own view away) is not told by the browser, so the pointer stays where it was. A thing that is gone a moment later is sometimes told without its place: the trace then says the thing was gone before its place could be read. A press in a window that is behind another window is only in the trace (behind another window), and the pointer waits on the part of that window you can see. Typing is shown for the box that has the keyboard, and not while you use that same window yourself. Firefox is not followed.

Checked on a real screen (Chrome 157, a test page pressed through UI Automation in a window that keeps itself on top): in four runs every press of a thing that stayed at least 150 ms was in the trace at the centre of that thing, and a picture shows the pointer on the pressed link, still there after the page had a new title. Real Gmail was only listened to, never pressed for a test: of 5 presses on a row of mail Chrome told 3 with the place, 1 without, and 1 not at all; a mark as unread press was never told.
Not checked: Edge worked through the screen, a screen that is not at 100% size, clicks in another steered browser than Edge, and a full Windows restart.
